speaker: Doctor
text: That is an interesting start; could you describe the nature of the hematuria and flank pain, and when did these symptoms first begin?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. To better understand the severity and potential cause, have you noticed any fever, chills, or nausea accompanying the flank pain? Also, is the pain sharp and colicky, or does it feel like a dull ache?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy and urine culture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis Findings: Appearance is Reddish. Leukocyte Esterase is Positive. White Blood Cells are 10-20 /HPF. Red Blood Cells are Too numerous to count. Nitrites are Negative.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the urinalysis showing significant pyuria and negative nitrites, do you have a known history of kidney stones or experience relief of the flank pain by changing positions? Also, have you noticed any fever or chills, which could suggest a complicated infection or abscess?

REQUEST TEST: Renal Ultrasound
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Pelvis_Imaging

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ultrasound Findings: Multiple cysts present in the collecting ducts of the medulla. No obstruction noted.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the ultrasound findings of medullary cysts combined with your history of recurrent UTIs and visible hematuria, I need to know if you have a known family history of kidney disease and whether you experience polyuria (excessive urination) or nocturia?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Medullary Sponge Kidney
